title: Evidence
description: Federal Rules of Evidence, Weeks 1–15 (Fisher, Evidence, 4th ed.): jury secrecy, relevance and 403, the policy exclusions, character evidence and 404(b), impeachment and the rape shield, hearsay and its exceptions, the Confrontation Clause, Bruton, the right to present a defense, lay and expert opinion, expert reliability, authentication and the best evidence rule, and privileges. Includes the outline, rule chart, flowcharts, flashcards, and bar-style practice questions.

Evidence_Condensed_Outline.docx.title: Evidence Outline
Evidence_Condensed_Outline.docx.description: Condensed exam outline of Weeks 1–15 on the Fall 2026 syllabus (Fisher pp. 1–1098). Part I covers the Federal Rules, jury secrecy under 606(b), relevance, conditional relevance, and 403. Part II covers the specialized relevance rules, 407–411. Part III covers character evidence: the propensity ban, 404(b), Huddleston, 413–415, the defendant's and victim's character, and habit. Part IV covers impeachment under 607–609 and the rape shield. Part V covers competency, the definition of hearsay, opposing parties' statements, prior statements of witnesses, and the 803, 804, and 807 exceptions. Part VI covers the Confrontation Clause from Crawford through Smith v. Arizona. Part VII covers completeness, Bruton, and Chambers. Part VIII covers lay and expert opinion from the Week 10 reading. Part IX covers expert bases and reliability (703, 705, Frye, Daubert, Joiner, Kumho Tire). Part X covers authentication and the best evidence rule (901–902, 1001–1008). Part XI covers Rule 501, the psychotherapist and lawyer-client privileges, 502 waiver, government lawyers, and self-incrimination. Part XII covers the spousal and marital-confidences privileges. Rule and tip boxes throughout, and a card for every principal case with its class.

Evidence_Master_Outline.docx.description: Full master outline of Weeks 1–15: Classes 1–19 swept against all 19 slide decks and the Week 1–10 readings, plus Parts IX–XII from the Week 11–15 readings, with every problem, the slides' answers, a syllabus coverage map, and an errata log. Kept off the public site. Use it as the reference when making questions, flowcharts, and flashcards for this subject.

2Evidence_Rule_Chart (with class slides).title: Evidence Rule Chart/outline
2Evidence_Rule_Chart (with class slides).description: The master rule chart for Weeks 1–5. Each rule is explained in plain English with a note on what to watch out for. Rows tagged by class come from the Class 1–10 lecture slides, and there are notes on what the midterm covers.

Federal_Rules_of_Evidence.html.title: Federal Rules of Evidence
Federal_Rules_of_Evidence.html.description: The full official text of all 69 Federal Rules of Evidence, as amended to December 1, 2024, with notes on the 2023 and 2024 amendments and the Rule 801(d)(1)(A) amendment taking effect December 1, 2026. Search by word, phrase, or cite (type 803(2) to go straight to the excited-utterance exception, or 404(b)(2) to see that clause marked), filter to the rules the course covers or to any of eleven course topics, and follow cross-references between rules. Each rule shows how often the outline and the practice sets cite it. The practice sets use it for their Look up popup: any rule cited in a question or explanation opens its text with the cited subdivision marked.

Evidence_Rule_Flowcharts.html.title: Evidence Flowcharts
Evidence_Rule_Flowcharts.html.description: Interactive decision charts for Weeks 1–5. Zoom and pan around each chart, walk through a rule one step at a time, and search all nine charts. Covers relevance (401–403), the policy rules (407–411), character evidence, 404(b), impeachment, 609 convictions, the 412 rape shield, and 606(b) jury secrecy.

FRE_Rule_Cards.html.title: FRE Rule Cards
FRE_Rule_Cards.html.description: Flashcards for the Federal Rules of Evidence in Weeks 1–5. Pick your topics, flip each card, and rate yourself with a tap or a swipe. Missed cards come back sooner, and your mastery is saved in your browser.

Evidence_MCQ_Conceptual.html.title: Evidence Rules easy Drill
Evidence_MCQ_Conceptual.html.description: Conceptual multiple-choice questions for Weeks 1–5, weighted toward the Federal Rules. The answer order reshuffles every time you load the page, so you can't memorize the letters.

Evidence_MCQ_Application (strict).html.title: Evidence BAR style questions 1
Evidence_MCQ_Application (strict).html.description: Bar-level application questions for Weeks 1–5. Each question sets two or three rules against each other and turns on a single fact. Every answer choice has its own explanation, and the set includes one-fact variations and a coverage map.

Evidence_MCQ_Application (Classes 1-10)..title: Evidence BAR style questions 2
Evidence_MCQ_Application (Classes 1-10)..description: A second, all-new set of bar-style application questions covering Classes 1–10. Every answer choice has its own explanation. Includes one-fact variations and a coverage map of all 157 outline items.

Evidence_Mock_Midterm.html.title: Evidence Mock Midterm
Evidence_Mock_Midterm.html.description: A timed practice exam for the night before the midterm: 60 new bar-style questions on Classes 1–10, in four 15-question parts that each cover every topic at the real exam’s 30-minute pace. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.

Evidence_Mock_Midterm_II.html.title: Evidence Mock Midterm II
Evidence_Mock_Midterm_II.html.description: A second timed practice exam: 60 more new bar-style questions on Classes 1–10, with no fact patterns repeated from the first. It has the same four 15-question parts, each covering every topic at the real exam’s 30-minute pace, and draws on textbook problems the first exam didn’t use. Answers stay hidden until you submit. Then you get your score by topic, the rules to review, and an explanation for every choice.

Evidence_Hearsay_Practice_Exam.html.title: Hearsay Practice Exam
Evidence_Hearsay_Practice_Exam.html.description: 41 bar-style questions, five choices each, covering all of hearsay: the definition and non-truth uses, opposing-party statements, prior statements and impeachment (613, 806), the 803 and 804 exceptions, 807, multiple hearsay, completeness under 106, and the Confrontation Clause through Smith v. Arizona and Samia. Includes the 2023 and 2024 amendments. Tutor mode grades each question as you go; timed mode gives you 80 minutes and grades at the end with a score by topic. Every question has the rule, an analysis, and why each choice is right or wrong.

Evidence_Concepts_Test.html.title: Evidence Concepts Test
Evidence_Concepts_Test.html.description: A 116-question concepts test on the whole course, Weeks 1–15, in outline order: jury secrecy, relevance and 403, the policy rules (407–411), character evidence, 404(b), and 413–415, impeachment and the rape shield, the hearsay definition, 801(d), and the 803–807 exceptions, the Confrontation Clause through Smith v. Arizona, completeness, Bruton, and the right to present a defense, lay and expert opinion through Daubert and Kumho Tire, authentication and the best evidence rule, and the lawyer-client, psychotherapist, and spousal privileges. Each question turns on a holding, an element, or a recent amendment, and its wrong choices are the dissents, overruled cases, and older rules students mix up. Five choices each. Tutor mode grades as you go; timed mode gives you 90 seconds a question. Every question has the rule, an analysis, and why each choice is right or wrong.
